DRAFT FOR OWNER REVIEW - NOT APPROVED OR PUBLISHED

This proposal is not adopted customer terms and must not be displayed as approved checkout terms. The selected Stripe provider, captured-payment-before-supplier rule and current 15% default markup remain unchanged. The choices below are proposed, not user-approved.

1. Initial merchandise and ordering. Proposed first release: a limited selection of authorized, new, standard parcel-shippable hardware. Each listing must show the exact manufacturer part, included items, applicable manufacturer warranty and any product-specific restrictions. Software subscriptions, custom configurations, oversized freight and government purchase orders stay in the quote workflow until their terms and fulfillment are separately validated. Stock is not reserved by viewing a listing or adding it to a cart.

2. Prices and payment. Display the full merchandise, shipping and tax total before consent. Do not increase the charge, substitute a product or change a destination after payment without the buyer's agreement. Verify captured payment before requesting a supplier purchase. A payment or order acknowledgment is not shipment confirmation. If the item cannot be supplied, contact the buyer promptly and issue the applicable refund; do not demand a second payment to clear a hold.

3. Shipping and delays. Display a supportable shipment estimate based on current supplier information; do not promise same-day dispatch or guaranteed delivery without evidence. If the stated shipment time cannot be met, notify the buyer and obtain the required consent to a revised shipment date or provide the required cancellation and prompt refund. Do not treat silence as consent to an indefinite delay. Partial shipments, substitutions and backorders require a separately supported workflow and clear buyer agreement.

4. Cancellation. Proposed commercial policy: accept cancellation requests before supplier release without a cancellation fee. After a supplier request is submitted, first verify whether it can be stopped; do not claim cancellation or a refund has occurred until confirmed. Supplier submission alone does not remove applicable buyer rights when shipment cannot be completed. This proposal does not authorize automatic refunds or adopt an undisclosed supplier fee.

5. Returns. Proposed starting policy, subject to supplier/OEM feasibility and owner approval: request a change-of-mind return within 30 calendar days after delivery for unopened standard hardware in original packaging. Obtain return authorization and the correct return address before sending goods. The buyer pays change-of-mind return shipping; Tri-Point pays the reasonable return-shipping cost for goods it supplied incorrectly or damaged. No restocking fee is proposed for eligible unopened standard items. Any exception must be reviewed and conspicuously disclosed before checkout, not added after purchase. Mandatory legal rights take priority.

6. Defects and warranty. Identify the manufacturer's actual warranty for each product before listing; do not invent a warranty period or imply an OEM warranty that is unavailable. Assist the buyer with incorrect, damaged or defective items and the applicable authorized warranty process. This draft does not waive statutory rights, impose a blanket 'as is' disclaimer or guarantee a resolution time the supplier has not confirmed.

7. Refund handling. Process approved or legally required refunds to the original payment method and communicate actual status. Do not describe a requested or pending refund as completed. For unshipped orders that must be refunded, include the applicable shipping and other amounts required by the circumstances. Implement the operational refund and delay-notification controls before public launch.

8. Taxes and exemptions. Determine collection obligations and exact product tax classifications from verified merchant information before enabling tax collection. Review exemption documentation through a secure process; government affiliation or a checkbox alone is not proof of exemption. A supplier resale certificate is not a blanket customer-sales exemption. No tax registration, zero-tax treatment or tax approval is asserted in this draft.

9. Buyer access and support. Guest, account or combined purchasing remains an owner decision. Existing one-order test invitations are not verified customer accounts. Give buyers a usable contact and secure order-status path; do not send payment secrets or private order-access links to an unverified address. Proposed support contact: alorenzo@tripointgs.com. Do not promise a response-time guarantee until staffing is approved.

OPEN DECISIONS: launch assortment and shipping geography; returns window and supplier-funded feasibility; tax headquarters and registrations; guest/account model; refund/delay handling; approval of final customer-facing wording. This proposal grants no public-release permission.
shippingNotes: PROPOSAL ONLY. Start with standard parcel-shippable hardware delivered within the contiguous United States, using the exact supported destination and supplier service. Charge the displayed verified shipping amount and do not silently increase it. No blanket free shipping, same-day shipment, guaranteed arrival, split-shipment or backorder promise. Confirm whether residential addresses and PO boxes are supported. Any proposed geography and service restriction requires owner approval and implementation. Supplier freight estimates are not guarantees of final invoiced cost. Required shipping-delay notices and refunds must be operational before launch.
taxNotes: NOT REVIEWED OR APPROVED. Obtain the actual tax headquarters address and current registration evidence through a secure source; do not assume the public website address is the tax headquarters. Confirm Florida registration and any other collection obligations, then review the exact selected SKU/manufacturer-part classifications. Stripe Tax settings, registrations and the site's approval flag are separate facts. Do not replace missing tax information with zero tax. Review exemptions securely. No registration numbers, certificates, credentials or private tax documents belong in the public repository. Exact products remain empty until verified.
